clue.text: Further help provided indirectly

parts.note: second as an adjective means further or additional, as in a second helping
a hand is help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: Someone receives additional assistance, though it reaches them through a go-between.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided' joins the wordplay to the definition 'indirectly': news heard secondhand comes through someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Something learnt secondhand comes via an intermediary rather than straight from the source.

clue.text: Round Charlie's playing, with piano introduction

indicators.note: introduction here means putting something in, so the piano letter is introduced among the others
playing suggests the letters of the name are being played about with and rearranged

parts.note: the name with its possessive s supplies all eight letters
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Charlie performs a round, a sung canon, starting off with a piano part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges CHARLIES (the S of the possessive counts) into SHERICAL, and 'introduction' slips P in after the S. 'Round' is not the song but the shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball-shaped object is round in every direction, the geometric sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Wheedle drinks, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase says the word for drinks is only heard, and a same-sounding word is written

parts.note: Cokes are cola drinks

explanation.surface: Someone sweet-talks their way into getting drinks bought for them.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheedle is to persuade gently with flattery, the same as to cajole.

clue.text: No chance it will be seen as silly to phone about article?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the scrambled letters surround the article
silly signals that the letters of the following words are muddled up

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A joke question: is ringing round about an item something nobody would bother with?
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' turns TO PHONE into NOTHOPE, and 'about' puts it around A after the T. 'it will be seen as' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something has not the slightest prospect is an idiom for no chance at all.

clue.text: Pension books entrusted to man over fifty

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above, so the earlier letters come before fifty
something entrusted to a person is placed in their keeping, so the books go inside the man

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
OT is the Old Testament, the first group of books of the Bible
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Retirement money in the form of books is handed over to a man past fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pension' is not retirement income here but the continental word for a boarding house, a small hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: In France and elsewhere a pension is a modest guest house, a type of lodging.

clue.text: Easy to appear wild

definitions.meaning: an easy, unforced manner is described as relaxed and unaffected
plants growing wild are untouched by human cultivation

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both an unaffected, relaxed manner and things existing in nature without cultivation.

clue.text: Do refuse dill flower

indicators.note: to do something over can mean to wreck or mess it up, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn down the herb dill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' at the front is the anagram signal, rearranging REFUSE DILL; 'flower' is the definition, not part of the herb picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The stylised lily of French heraldry is named after a flower, literally a lily.

clue.text: Bottom line?

parts.note: the phrase reads like the final figure in accounts, but means literally the line printed at the foot of a page

explanation.definitionFit: Text running along the base of a document page is the lowest line on it.

clue.text: Rex in new production of Iolanthe — brave guy

indicators.note: in tells us the king's letter goes inside the rearranged title
a new production restages the opera, so its title letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king appears in a fresh staging of the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, playing a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new production of' rearranges IOLANTHE (a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera) and R goes in, giving LIONHEART.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard I was nicknamed for his courage, and the epithet is used for any very courageous person.

clue.text: Carry note about occupational therapist

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the note goes round the therapist

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A message is passed round a hospital therapist.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote something is to lug or haul it around.

clue.text: Standing before performance leads to improvement

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second in the across answer

parts.note: someone standing is up, out of bed or on their feet
a turn is a performer's act on stage

explanation.surface: An ovation before the act results in better fortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' just joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise in fortunes or figures after a slump is a recovery or upswing.

clue.text: Smart about role re-assignment, being irascible

indicators.note: about places the stylish word around the rearranged letters

parts.note: chic means smart and stylish

indicators.note: re-assignment of a role suggests its letters being moved to new places

explanation.surface: Someone sharply dressed is bad-tempered about being moved to a different job.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a hot-tempered person who is quick to anger.

clue.text: Insouciance evident in flawed census, alas

indicators.note: a flawed version is a faulty one, signalling these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A population count with errors shows carelessness, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evident in' only links the definition to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Insouciance is a nonchalant lack of concern, an offhand unconcern.

clue.text: Run straight

definitions.meaning: to run a business or production is to manage or conduct it
a straight route or answer is one without deviation or evasion

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to manage or control; as an adjective it means going without a detour, frank.

clue.text: Correspondence read religiously?

parts.note: letters read devotedly are, taken literally, the New Testament letters read aloud in church services

explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament letters of Paul and others are read as lessons in Christian worship.

clue.text: Flyer, a stirrer put on a charge

indicators.note: in a down clue, put on means set on top, so this piece comes first

parts.note: a spoon is a utensil for stirring
a bill is a charge for goods or services

explanation.surface: A troublemaker is arrested and charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirrer' suggests a troublemaker and 'charge' an arrest, but these are kitchen and invoice words; 'Flyer' is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The wading bird with the flattened, spatulate bill is something that flies.

clue.text: Issue involving publicity stunt

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the advert goes inside the other word

parts.note: to issue is to flow out, as gas does when it escapes
an ad is publicity

explanation.surface: A matter arising from a publicity stunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A daring or mischievous adventure is a prank or caper.

clue.text: Bar code?

parts.note: the shop barcode becomes the code of language used by barristers, the Bar being the legal profession

explanation.definitionFit: Lawyers' jargon, the specialised language of the courts, is the vocabulary of the legal profession.

clue.text: Short of energy before collapse

indicators.note: before places the energy word ahead of the other piece

parts.note: go means energy or vigour
under means short of, as in under a mile

explanation.surface: Someone running out of steam just before they keel over.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that fails or a swimmer who sinks is said to founder, the same as this phrase.

clue.text: Style article written about Italian city .

parts.note: a mode is a style or fashion

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the article is written backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fashion piece written on an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks as if it means 'concerning', but it turns AN round to NA.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in northern Italy, in Emilia-Romagna, famous for balsamic vinegar and fast cars.

clue.text: Extract ten pence out of Frank?

indicators.note: out of indicates the letters for ten and pence are taken from the longer word

parts.note: frank means outspoken, explicit
X is the Roman numeral ten and p the abbreviation for pence

explanation.surface: Getting a small coin from a man called Frank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name, but is the adjective meaning outspoken; removing X and P from EXPLICIT leaves ELICIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit information is to draw it out of someone.

clue.text: Possible upshot — a point for boxer

indicators.note: possible suggests a potential new arrangement of the letters

parts.note: W is west, a compass point

explanation.surface: A likely outcome, and one point awarded to a fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' rearranges UPSHOT and A into SOUTHPA, then W follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A southpaw is a left-handed fighter in the ring, leading with the right.

clue.text: Lake crossed by Arthur once

indicators.note: the lake is said to be crossed by the words, so it spans the gap between them

explanation.surface: King Arthur once sailed across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Great Lakes of North America, on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: Key evidence involving navy officer

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the navy letter is held inside

parts.note: E is a musical key
a sign is an indication or evidence

explanation.surface: Crucial proof implicates a naval officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' is a musical key, E, not 'crucial'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a junior commissioned rank in the US Navy and an old army rank.

clue.text: See husband before giving present

indicators.note: before places the husband letter first

parts.note: ere is an old word meaning before, the clue's second before being read through giving

explanation.surface: Seeing a husband before handing over a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in attendance or at hand is a sense of present as an adjective.

clue.text: Demand right away to see European banker

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is removed

parts.note: to order is to demand

explanation.surface: Insisting on seeing a European bank official immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is a river, which has banks; the ODER runs between Germany and Poland. 'right away' looks like 'immediately'.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a banker in crossword terms, something with banks; this one flows through central Europe.

clue.text: Services site, one mostly meant for redevelopment

indicators.note: redevelopment of a site rebuilds it, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A motorway services site, mainly earmarked for being rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts MEANT to MEAN; SITE, I and MEAN are then rearranged by 'for redevelopment'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenities are the facilities provided in a place, the services offered.

clue.text: Zest for making marmalade?

parts.note: zest reads as enthusiasm, but means the grated skin of a citrus fruit used in the preserve

explanation.definitionFit: Zest is the outer rind of citrus fruit, and the bitter rind goes into marmalade.
